# Achromatic lens (`achromatic_lens`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/physics.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Physics, optics & astronomy (`physics`)
- Deps: needs lenses, clear_glass, spectrum_colour
- Core idea: A single lens focuses blue light nearer than red, so images have coloured edges. Two lenses of different glass cemented or mounted together cancel most of this: a convex lens of ordinary (crown) glass with a weaker concave lens of heavy lead (flint) glass, which spreads colours about twice as strongly for the same bending. The pair still focuses, but red and blue now meet. This makes short, sharp telescopes and, later, good microscopes and camera lenses.
- Pitfalls:
  - Using two lenses of the same glass (cannot cancel colour)
  - Citing Newton, who wrongly concluded it was impossible
  - Underestimating the glass problem: streak-free flint glass was the bottleneck until Guinand and Fraunhofer
- History: europe: c. 1729–1733 – Chester Moor Hall has the first doublets made; 1758 John Dollond's patent and commercial production; c. 1805–1814 Guinand and Fraunhofer make large homogeneous flint glass; 1830 J. J. Lister's achromatic microscope
- Read:
  - John Dollond, An Account of Some Experiments Concerning the Different Refrangibility of Light, Philosophical Transactions 50 (1758)
  - Henry C. King, The History of the Telescope (1955)
